correctness.rationale: The original source incorrectly claimed uniqueness of an eligible sorted index. Independent counterexample a=(1,1), G=(1,3), g=2 yields tau_1=B1/A1=3 and tau_2=B2/A2=3, so both k=1 and k=2 meet rho_k<=tau_k<=rho_(k+1). This refutes the stated index uniqueness, but not the optimization. Fully corrected RESULT.md, REVIEW.md and VERIFICATION.md replace that assertion with the first eligible k convention and explicit tie handling. In logarithmic variables y=log r the objective is strictly convex (the g>0 term gives the second log-sum-exp a zero exponent vector) and coercive; KKT yields r_i=max(1,sqrt(rho_i/tau)), sorted clamping, and tau=B_k/A_k. The weighted-average recurrence proves existence of the first admissible k. All admissible indices describe the same unique r, and minimum (sqrt(Ak Bk)+sum_{i>k}sqrt(a_i G_i))^2; ceiling increases only first factor by <=2. At the tie example F(1,1)=12, exactly both formulas. Full final scientific files were created with exact original blob guards and UTF-8 SHA-256, and the corrected final claim was reassessed.
